what_happened: On job 20261014-192705-j4be, a prompts-related request, the user corrected Athena's accepted reading 1. The corrected version says the self-grading rule must be enforced in code, not only in prompts. Under it, Athena itself flags any candidate that moves a requirements-map row to Covered as a major finding. The stored fields don't include the original wording. The correction implies it left the rule as prompt guidance with no code check behind it. The user said the reading did not match what they meant.
cause: Athena treats prompt instructions as enough to carry a rule, even when the rule guards against the model's own conflict of interest, such as a candidate grading its own work. Nothing in the defaults says that a rule about self-grading or integrity must be enforced by code that does not depend on the model's compliance. So a prompt-only reading looks complete and was accepted. Only the user's correction exposed the gap.
prevention: Add a default for readings: when a request concerns a rule that stops Athena or a candidate from grading or approving its own work, the reading must name a code-level check as a deliverable. It must also add an acceptance criterion that a violating change is flagged by that check without any model judgment. Prompt wording alone is never enough for such rules.
proposed_request: Enforce the self-grading rule in code, not only in prompts. When a candidate change moves any row in the requirements map to Covered, Athena itself must detect this in code and record it as a major finding, without relying on the model's judgment or on prompt wording. Acceptance: a test or fixture where a candidate flips a requirements-map row to Covered produces a major finding. A candidate that leaves rows unchanged, or that moves a row to a status other than Covered, produces none. Keep the existing prompt wording and make sure it matches the code behavior.
